definitions.explanation: An expression telling someone to be careful or take care. Often used when someone is leaving. Comes from {気|き}をつける (to pay attention, to be careful).

examples.japanese: {気|き}をつけて{行|い}ってきてね。
examples.english: Take care and have a good trip.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}に{気|き}をつけてください。
{足元|あしもと}に{気|き}をつけて。
{夜|よる}{道|みち}は{暗|くら}いから、{気|き}をつけてね。
examples.english: The streets are dark at night, so be careful.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}から{旅行|りょこう}ですね。{体|からだ}に{気|き}をつけて{楽|たの}しんできてください。
examples.english: Your trip starts tomorrow, right? Take care of yourself and enjoy it.

notes: 気をつけて is the te-form of 気をつける used as a farewell or warning. It's commonly said when someone is leaving on a trip or going out. The polite form is 気をつけてください. It can also be used as a warning about specific dangers.
